keyTerms.definition: The record of which sources each lesson concept comes from.
A single named idea that the lesson teaches.

recall.question: Does this lesson reproduce the instructor's lectures?
recall.answer: No. It is locally authored bridge content and does not claim to reproduce the lectures.

keyTerms.definition: The set of topics this lesson covers.
A skill the learner can show after the lesson.

recall.question: What must a learner be able to do after this lesson?
recall.answer: Name every object with its unit and shape, compute a toy by hand and in code, check it with an assertion, and state what breaks when one rule drops.

keyTerms.definition: The question that names the gap the new idea must fill.
An example that runs the same objects through the numbers.

recall.question: What closes every section?
recall.answer: Code, checks, costs, alternatives, and a failure case close each section.

keyTerms.definition: A bag of distinct items where order does not matter.
A rule that maps each input to exactly one output.
The set of allowed inputs to a function.
The set of outputs a function produces.

recall.question: What is the one-line contract of a function?
recall.answer: Each input maps to exactly one output.

recall.question: Why does training break when one input has two targets?
recall.answer: No squared-error update can satisfy two different targets for one input at once.

keyTerms.definition: Compressed language where each symbol has a fixed contract.
The fixed meaning of a symbol: what it takes and returns.

recall.question: How do you read a formula fast?
recall.answer: Learn each symbol's contract once: what it means, what it takes, what it returns. Then read fast forever.

keyTerms.definition: A noun attached to a number, like meters or dollars.
The rule: tag every term with its unit.

recall.question: Why must you never add 800 sq ft and 320 thousand dollars?
recall.answer: The sum 1120 has no unit and no meaning. Only quantities with the same unit may add.

recall.question: What does the slope's unit tell you?
recall.answer: Each extra square foot adds about 433 dollars to the price.

keyTerms.definition: One number made by piling all items of a list together.
One number made by scaling a running total, one factor at a time.
A product growing past the largest float and becoming infinity.

recall.question: Why do products amplify single changes more than sums?
recall.answer: Changing 7 to 9 moved the sum by 2 but the product by 20.

recall.question: What is the product of an empty list, and why?
recall.answer: 1 by convention. Starting a product accumulator at 0 always returns 0.

keyTerms.definition: A count of orders of smallness; log10(0.1) equals -1.
A tiny product rounding to 0.0 in float arithmetic.
Working with logs of values instead of the values, to keep numbers finite.
The sum of log probabilities, one term per data point.

recall.question: Why does 0.1 to the 400th power compute as 0.0?
recall.answer: The true value is positive but far below the smallest representable float, so it underflows.

recall.question: What is the rule for comparing models with log-likelihoods?
recall.answer: Do not exponentiate back. Compare in log space.

keyTerms.definition: One object that packs a list of numbers, with direction and length.
The length of a vector, computed with Pythagoras.
The sum of pairwise item products of two vectors.

recall.question: How does scaling a vector change its length?
recall.answer: It scales by the same factor: the norm of 3v is 3 times the norm of v.

recall.question: What goes wrong adding vectors of different lengths?
recall.answer: It has no meaning. Code must fail loudly, never guess.

keyTerms.definition: One direction of a table: axis 0 runs down rows, axis 1 across columns.
An operation that collapses one axis and deletes it from the shape.

recall.question: What shape results from summing a (2,3) table along axis 0?
recall.answer: Shape (3,): the 2 rows collapse into 1 row of 3 column totals.

recall.question: What is the silent failure with axis means?
recall.answer: Taking the mean over the wrong axis gives wrong numbers with no error raised.

keyTerms.definition: The smallest code version of a formula, with known answers.
A statement of what must be true; the program stops and names the line if it is false.

recall.question: What does a passing test prove?
recall.answer: Only the tested cases. It does not prove the function works for other inputs.

recall.question: What does deleting the sqrt line teach?
recall.answer: The test compares 25.0 to 5.0 and fails, naming the exact wrong value, so the fix is obvious.

keyTerms.definition: The shown range of an axis; part of the plot's claim.
A plot whose axes start at 0 and whose labels carry units.

recall.question: How does truncating the y-axis to [300, 750] lie?
recall.answer: The eye reads a 2.3x price range as a 10x range. The story flips from steady climb to explosive growth.

recall.question: What are the correctness checks for the scatter plot?
recall.answer: Count 6 dots, read one dot against its data row, axes start at 0, labels name the units.

keyTerms.definition: A guard at a door: every value that passes has shown its papers.
The allowed gap in a float comparison, like 1e-9.

recall.question: Where should an assertion catch a wrong number?
recall.answer: At the exact line where it goes wrong, before it corrupts downstream numbers.

recall.question: Why is tol=1e-16 a bad tolerance?
recall.answer: It fails on legitimate float noise and trains the team to delete assertions.

keyTerms.definition: A float format with about 7 decimal digits of precision.
A float format with about 16 decimal digits of precision.
Losing all significant digits when subtracting nearly equal large numbers.

recall.question: Why does (1e16 + 1) - 1e16 equal 0.0 in float64?
recall.answer: Sixteen digits of budget cannot hold a 1 seventeen digits down from the leading digit, so the sum rounds back to 1e16.

recall.question: When is float32 the right choice?
recall.answer: Large-scale training where memory and speed matter. Use float64 for learning and debugging numerics.

keyTerms.definition: A number that fixes a random generator's whole sequence.
The property that the same code gives the same answer twice.

recall.question: What happens when you seed inside the training loop?
recall.answer: The generator resets each iteration, so every batch draws the first random numbers and the data order never varies.

recall.question: What is the seeding discipline?
recall.answer: Seed once at the start, log the seed with the results, never seed inside a loop.

keyTerms.definition: One stored object per value: name, unit, shape, check.
A few seconds of checking per quantity buys back hours of silent wrong numbers.

recall.question: What is the U01 rule in one line?
recall.answer: A few seconds of naming and checking per quantity buys back hours of silent wrong numbers.

keyTerms.definition: A question the learner answers by hand and in code.
The file with worked answers, at lessons/u01/keys.md.

recall.question: Where are the answers to E01-E27?
recall.answer: In lessons/u01/keys.md.

sections.title: Deep oral ladders (questions. Answers in lessons/u01/keys.md)

keyTerms.definition: A chain of questions that climbs from definition to critique.
The functions ladder: define, compute, code, compare, debug, critique.

recall.question: What are the rungs of ladder L01?
recall.answer: Define a function, say the C01 toy in your own words, show f(3), code the mapping and its check, compare to relations, debug the duplicate key, critique the contract.

keyTerms.definition: The debug task: a norm function that fails one of three lesson tests.
The defect the learner must find, fix, and attribute to a test.

recall.question: What must you state after fixing D01?
recall.answer: Which test caught the bug.

keyTerms.definition: The scenario that adds a rooms feature, turning houses into vectors.
The scenario that asks whether 400 factors of 0.99 still underflow.

recall.question: What does S02 ask you to decide?
recall.answer: Whether the direct product still underflows at 400 factors of 0.99, and when you would still choose log space.

keyTerms.definition: The critique question attacking the claim that float32 is always fine for ML.
A float format with about 7 decimal digits of precision.

recall.question: What does R01 demand?
recall.answer: Two computed counterexamples from the lesson against the float32 claim, plus the precise conditions where float32 is safe.

keyTerms.definition: An original PNG rendered with matplotlib and read back for verification.
The honest-axes scatter plot: six dots, axes from zero, labeled with units.

recall.question: How was f09 verified?
recall.answer: Rendered with matplotlib 3.6.3 at dpi 150, opened and read on 2026-10-06.

keyTerms.definition: Concepts not yet understood, each with a named home in a later lesson.
The later pass that will build local bridges for each listed concept.

recall.question: Name two items on the dependency list and their homes.
recall.answer: Formal limit definition of the derivative, needed for U03. Matrix multiplication mechanics, needed for U02.
